title: CrossModal Study
description: EEG dataset from a cross-modal cueing study in which participants were cued to prepare for an auditory, visual, or non-specific target. A 3-second task-irrelevant delay followed the cue, during which a fixation cross was frequency-tagged at 36 Hz and a 40 Hz amplitude-modulated tone was played. Participants discriminated one of three gabor-patch or tone targets, sometimes with a distractor from the uncued modality. The dataset supports investigation of alpha oscillations and target preparation in cross-modal attention.
methods_description: Healthy participants with normal or corrected-to-normal vision performed a cued target-discrimination task with six randomized, balanced conditions (non-specific, auditory, or visual cue, with or without a distractor) across 28 blocks after 36 practice trials. EEG was recorded with an additional EOG channel. Recordings took place at the University of Birmingham, UK. Participants responded with arrow keys to identify tone pitch or gabor-patch orientation.
